\subsection*{Randomized --- BPOperator: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.BPOperator}.

\subsection*{Randomized --- BPOperator: Results}

\begin{definition}[Reductions to a language class]
\lean{Randomized.BPdot}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p015-b002}
\label{Randomized.BPdot}
\leanok
For a set $\mathcal{C}$ of languages over the Boolean alphabet, the associated class
consists of all Boolean languages $L$ for which there is some $C\in\mathcal{C}$ such
that $L\leq_r C$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reflexivity of randomized reducibility]
\lean{Randomized.RandReducible.refl}
\label{Randomized.RandReducible.refl}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Randomized.RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible}
\difficulty{1}
Every language of bit strings is randomized reducible to itself.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Class inclusion in its randomized closure]
\lean{Randomized.subset_BPdot}
\label{Randomized.subset_BPdot}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPdot, Randomized.RandReducible.refl}
\difficulty{1}
For any set $\mathcal{C}$ of languages, every language in $\mathcal{C}$ belongs to the
class of languages that reduce randomly to some member of $\mathcal{C}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of randomized reductions]
\lean{Randomized.BPdot_mono}
\label{Randomized.BPdot_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPdot}
\difficulty{1}
For any two classes of languages $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ with $\mathcal{C}
\subseteq \mathcal{D}$, every language that reduces by a many-one reduction to some
language in $\mathcal{C}$ also reduces by a many-one reduction to some language in
$\mathcal{D}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Composition of randomized and polynomial reductions]
\lean{Randomized.RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible_right}
\label{Randomized.RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible_right}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Randomized.randProb_congr}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$, $B$, and $C$ be languages of bit strings. If $A$ is randomized reducible to $B$
and $B$ is polynomial-time reducible to $C$, then $A$ is randomized reducible to $C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized reductions from NP]
\lean{Randomized.BPdot_NP_eq_BPNP}
\label{Randomized.BPdot_NP_eq_BPNP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.SAT3, Complexity.SAT3_NPHard, Complexity.SAT3_mem_NP, Randomized.BPNP, Randomized.BPdot, Randomized.RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible_right}
\difficulty{3}
The class of languages that reduce by a many-one reduction to some language in NP equals
the class of languages that reduce by a many-one reduction to 3-SAT.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized reductions to P]
\lean{Randomized.BPdot_P_eq_BPP}
\label{Randomized.BPdot_P_eq_BPP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Randomized.BPdot, Randomized.InBPP, Randomized.InBPP.of_randReducible, Randomized.boolVerifier, Randomized.inBPP_polyTimeModel_of_mem_P, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.randProb_mono, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
The class of languages that reduce by a many-one reduction to some language in P equals
the class of languages decidable by polynomial-time randomized verifiers with success
probability at least $2/3$ on members and nonmembers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized closure of BPP under reductions]
\lean{Randomized.BPdot_BPP_eq_BPP}
\label{Randomized.BPdot_BPP_eq_BPP}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPdot, Randomized.InBPP, Randomized.InBPP.of_randReducible, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.subset_BPdot}
\difficulty{4}
The class of languages that reduce to some language in BPP by a many-one reduction
equals BPP.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized polynomial time via reductions]
\lean{Randomized.BPdot_P_eq_BPP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.BPdot_P_eq_BPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Randomized.BPP_PTM, Randomized.BPP_PTM_eq, Randomized.BPdot, Randomized.BPdot_P_eq_BPP}
\difficulty{3}
The class of languages that reduce by a many-one reduction to some language in P equals
the union, over all natural numbers $c$, of the classes decidable by bounded-error
randomized machines in time bounded by a constant multiple of $n \mapsto n^c+1$.
\end{theorem}
